title: Hydrogen bonding
body: Hydrogen bonding is the interaction that arises from the polarity of water's polar covalent H–O bonds; it occurs between adjacent water molecules and between and within biological molecules.
ced_evidence: 1.1.A.1 "This polarity contributes to hydrogen bonding between and within biological molecules"; 1.1.A.2 "hydrogen bonds between adjacent polar water molecules"

title: Illustrative polysaccharides
body: The CED's illustrative examples of polysaccharides (complex carbohydrates) built from monosaccharide monomers; their specific molecular structures are beyond the AP Exam.

items.label: Cellulose
items.meaning: Polysaccharide (complex carbohydrate) made of monosaccharide monomers joined by covalent bonds.

items.label: Starch
items.meaning: Polysaccharide (complex carbohydrate) made of monosaccharide monomers joined by covalent bonds.

items.label: Glycogen
items.meaning: Polysaccharide (complex carbohydrate) made of monosaccharide monomers joined by covalent bonds.

ced_evidence: EK 1.4.A.1 illustrative examples: "Cellulose, Starch, Glycogen"; "Monosaccharides (simple sugars) are the monomers for polysaccharides (complex carbohydrates)"

title: Dehydration synthesis
body: Dehydration synthesis joins two smaller molecules by covalent bonding when a hydrogen ion is removed from one monomer and a hydroxyl group from the other, which causes the loss of the equivalent of a water molecule; the connection of many monomers is polymerization.
ced_evidence: 1.3.A.2 "Dehydration synthesis occurs when two smaller molecules are joined together through covalent bonding"
